**certfan 0.3.0** — ask several DNS resolvers and probe every node any of them hands out.

GeoDNS, latency routing and split-horizon DNS give different clients different addresses, so a check from one
place only ever sees part of the fleet. The node that missed the reload is often the one your resolver never returns.

- **`--resolver IP[:PORT]`** (repeatable): query these resolvers instead of the system one and probe the union of
  their A/AAAA answers. Built-in stub DNS client (UDP, TCP fallback on truncation, all resolvers in parallel), so
  certfan is still zero-dependency.
- **Attribution:** each node records which resolvers returned it: `via 8.8.8.8` in text when answers differ,
  `resolvers` per node and `dns: {resolvers, errors, divergent}` per host in JSON, `certfan_dns_divergent{host}` in Prometheus.
- **`--dns-divergence note|warn|fail`** (default `note`): different answers are normal for GeoDNS, so by default they are
  only shown; use `warn` / `fail` when every resolver should agree (e.g. a decommissioned node still in one zone).
- A resolver that times out or SERVFAILs is a WARN; NXDOMAIN just means no addresses.

```bash
certfan check shop.example.com --resolver 1.1.1.1 --resolver 8.8.8.8 --resolver 10.0.0.2
```

Install: `pipx install "git+https://github.com/Blackman99/certfan@v0.3.0"` or the wheel below.
Zero dependencies, Python 3.9+.
